newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 lower Thursday in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were mainly lower, pressured by trade selling. Sterling's continued strength against marks weighed on the market too. At the midday break, September was down eight stg at 1,049 stg a tonne after peaking earlier at 1,061 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures ended broadly higher for the second straight session as the market continued to bounce back after its recent nine percent freefall. September settled up $16 at $1,594 a tonne after ranging from $1,598 to $1,575. Spot July gained the same to close at $1,572, while the remaining months finished $16 to $17 higher.

Technically, traders pegged near-term September support at around $1,580. They said filling a chart gap between Wednesday's high of $1,598 and $1,610 mark was still an upside objective for September, with the next level of resistance seen at $1,625.
